title: The Travelers Ecstasy Of Divine Unity

questions.question: In the first short poem, what image is used for the universe?
questions.answer: It is pictured like a written book full of meaning.

questions.question: What does the passage compare Allah’s power to when it speaks about what is written in that book?
questions.answer: It compares Allah’s power to a pen that writes beautiful signs.

questions.question: What does the poem say about the ability of a believing heart to notice Allah’s signs?
questions.answer: It says the heart can see clear proofs of Allah without being left in darkness or confusion.

questions.question: What does the passage suggest by saying the signs are written with light?
questions.answer: It suggests that the proofs are bright, clear, and easy to recognize for someone who reflects.

questions.question: In the next part, what does the passage say about the “pages” of the world’s book?
questions.answer: They are countless and stretch beyond measure.

questions.question: What are the “lines” in that book said to be?
questions.answer: They are the many events that happen through time.

questions.question: How is every created thing described in relation to meaning?
questions.answer: Each thing is presented like a meaningful word that shows a message.

questions.question: What central message do all things announce together?
questions.answer: They declare that only Allah deserves worship.

questions.question: Besides declaring Allah’s oneness, what two cries are mentioned together in harmony?
questions.answer: They call out to the True One and to the Living One.

questions.question: What does the passage say is found in all things?
questions.answer: A sign that points to Allah’s oneness.

questions.question: How do the heart and the nafs respond after hearing this message?
questions.answer: They both accept it and confirm that it is true.

questions.question: What is the main idea of the whole marked passage?
questions.answer: All of creation points clearly to the oneness of Allah.

questions.question: Why does the passage speak about the world as if it were a book?
questions.answer: To show that the world can be read for signs, lessons, and proofs.

questions.question: What do the written marks in this “book” stand for?
questions.answer: They stand for the created things and events in the universe.

questions.question: According to the passage, is there any hidden dark spot left for the heart’s sight? Explain.
questions.answer: No. The passage teaches that the signs are made clear enough for the heart to recognize.

questions.question: What does the passage teach about the amount of meaning in the world?
questions.answer: It teaches that the world holds endless layers of meaning and countless signs.

questions.question: What does the passage say about events in time?
questions.answer: It presents them as many works that are part of a greater meaningful record.

questions.question: What does it mean that every being is like an embodied word?
questions.answer: It means each created thing is a visible sign carrying a message from its Creator.

questions.question: When all things speak together, what belief are they united on?
questions.answer: They are united on the truth that Allah is One.

questions.question: Which quality of Allah is emphasized by the words calling on the Living One?
questions.answer: His everlasting life.

questions.question: What conclusion is drawn from the signs in every created thing?
questions.answer: That each thing points toward the unity of Allah.

questions.question: What lesson comes from the heart and nafs saying “yes” at the end?
questions.answer: A person’s inner self should recognize and submit to clear truth.

questions.question: What object from everyday reading is used to help explain the universe?
questions.answer: A book or written page.

questions.question: What is the role of the “pen” in the passage’s picture?
questions.answer: It represents divine power bringing signs and forms into existence.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the clarity of those signs to the heart?
questions.answer: It describes them as shining clearly before the heart’s understanding.

questions.question: What does the passage imply about someone who reflects carefully on creation?
questions.answer: Such a person can notice evidence of Allah in what he sees.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the amount of pages and writings in the world’s book?
questions.answer: It says they are beyond counting.

questions.question: What is the connection between time and the “lines” in the book image?
questions.answer: The happenings of time are pictured like lines written across the pages.

questions.question: What shared statement is made by all things in the passage?
questions.answer: They all witness that there is no god but Allah.

questions.question: What does the joined calling of all things show about the message of creation?
questions.answer: It shows that creation gives one united testimony.

questions.question: What key belief is directly stated near the end of the passage?
questions.answer: That Allah is One.

questions.question: How does the final response of the heart and nafs strengthen the passage’s message?
questions.answer: It shows that both reflection and inner recognition lead to accepting the truth.

questions.question: In the passage, what does the “cosmic book” idea teach about the universe?
questions.answer: It teaches that the universe can be understood as full of signs and messages.

questions.question: Who is shown as the One behind those signs?
questions.answer: Allah.

questions.question: Why does the passage mention the “heart’s eye” instead of only the physical eye?
questions.answer: Because recognizing these truths needs inner understanding, not just looking.

questions.question: What can be inferred from the statement that no dark point remains?
questions.answer: The signs of Allah are made very clear for anyone sincere in reflection.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the size and number of the world’s meanings?
questions.answer: It describes them as limitless and extremely many.

questions.question: What does the mention of a preserved record suggest about reality?
questions.answer: It suggests that creation is known, ordered, and meaningful, not accidental.

questions.question: What is every being said to be like in that record?
questions.answer: A meaningful word made visible in the world.

questions.question: What two names are called out together after the declaration of Allah’s oneness?
questions.answer: The True One and the Living One.

questions.question: What single truth does every thing contain a sign for?
questions.answer: The truth that Allah is One.

questions.question: How do the heart and nafs model the right response to these signs?
questions.answer: They listen, understand, and agree with the truth.

questions.question: What is one major symbol used throughout the marked passage?
questions.answer: The symbol of the world as a book.

questions.question: What does that symbol help us understand about created things?
questions.answer: That created things are like messages with meaning, not meaningless objects.

questions.question: In the poem, what writes the signs seen in the universe?
questions.answer: Divine power is described as writing them.

questions.question: What effect does this image have on the reader’s view of nature and the world?
questions.answer: It encourages the reader to see the world as full of evidence of Allah.

questions.question: According to the passage, are the signs in creation few or many? Explain.
questions.answer: They are many beyond counting, because the passage speaks of endless pages and countless works.

questions.question: How are events in time treated in the book image?
questions.answer: They are treated like written lines that carry meaning.

questions.question: Why is it important that every being is called meaningful?
questions.answer: Because it shows that everything has a purpose and points to truth.

questions.question: What statement do all things proclaim together?
questions.answer: They proclaim that none has the right to be worshipped except Allah.

questions.question: What does the passage mean by saying they speak “in unison” and “in harmony”?
questions.answer: It means all creation agrees in giving the same witness.

questions.question: What evidence for tawhid is mentioned in the line about every thing having a sign?
questions.answer: Every single created thing itself serves as evidence for Allah’s oneness.

questions.question: What inner faculties respond positively at the end of the passage?
questions.answer: The heart and the nafs.

questions.question: How does the passage connect seeing the world and believing in Allah?
questions.answer: It teaches that looking deeply at the world leads a person to signs of Allah’s unity.

questions.question: What does the image of a colored page add to the description of creation?
questions.answer: It adds the idea that creation is rich, beautiful, and full of variety.

questions.question: What does the passage teach about spiritual sight?
questions.answer: It teaches that the heart can perceive truths that lead to faith.

questions.question: What do the endless leaves and many lines suggest about the universe?
questions.answer: They suggest that the universe contains unending signs and lessons.

questions.question: What relationship does the passage show between beings and meaning?
questions.answer: It shows that every being carries meaning like a word in a message.

questions.question: What can a reader infer about the order of the world from the idea of a preserved record?
questions.answer: The world follows a known and purposeful order.

questions.question: What is the first declaration all things make together?
questions.answer: That there is no deity worthy of worship except Allah.

questions.question: What additional calls follow that declaration?
questions.answer: They call upon the True One and the Living One.

questions.question: Why is the phrase about a sign in every thing important for understanding the passage?
questions.answer: Because it sums up the message that all parts of creation point to one Creator.

questions.question: What change happens in the listener’s inner self by the end?
questions.answer: The inner self moves from hearing the message to affirming it.

questions.question: What is the best summary of the final line of the marked passage?
questions.answer: The person’s heart and self both accept the truth shown by creation.
